title: An Empirical Evaluation of Using Large Language Models for Automated Unit Test Generation
objective: Evaluate whether off-the-shelf LLMs can automatically generate useful unit tests with minimal manual effort; implement TESTPILOT.
prompt_strategy: Signature + optional function body, documentation, usage examples; adaptive retry includes failing test and error message.
metrics: Test success/failure; failure reasons; statement/branch coverage; assertion quality; similarity to existing tests.
compile_or_syntax_evidence: Validator checks syntactic validity; invalid tests are marked failed. Simple syntax errors may be repaired before execution.
execution_evidence: Generated tests are executed; failures include assertion failure, timeout/nontermination, and uncaught exceptions.
repair: RetryWithError includes the failing test and error message; applied once per prompt. Adaptive approach fixes on average 15.6% of failing tests.
main_result: gpt-3.5-turbo median statement coverage 70.2% and branch coverage 52.8%; median 61.4% of tests include non-trivial assertions.
failure_categories: Syntactic invalidity; assertion failure; timeout/nontermination; uncaught/runtime exception; framework-completion issues.
limitations: 25 npm packages; JavaScript-only implementation; may not generalize to other languages/proprietary code; snippet matching is heuristic.
rq_relevance: Very high for failure-stage separation and exactly-one error-feedback retry precedent.

title: ASTER: Natural and Multi-Language Unit Test Generation with LLMs
objective: Develop a generic static-analysis-guided LLM pipeline for compilable, high-coverage and natural unit tests across Java and Python.
dataset: Java SE: Commons CLI/Codec/Compress/JXPath; Java EE: CargoTracker, DayTrader, PetClinic and App X; large Python benchmark.
language_framework: Java + Python; Java testing-framework and mocking context detected/configured.
models: GPT-4-turbo; Llama3-70B; CodeLlama-34B; Granite-34B; Llama3-8B; Granite-8B.
prompt_strategy: Static analysis supplies testing scope, constructors, auxiliary methods, call chains and mocking context.
metrics: Line/branch/method coverage; naturalness; developer survey; compile/runtime remediation.
compile_or_syntax_evidence: Postprocessing handles non-parsable output, framework mismatch, missing imports/package/class/folder details, and compilation issues.
execution_evidence: Generated tests are checked for runtime errors; failing tests include assertion/runtime failures.
repair: Rule-based sanitization/context recovery followed by test-repair prompts for compilation/runtime errors; coverage augmentation follows.
main_result: ASTER is competitive with EvoSuite on Java SE and substantially better on Java EE; developer survey strongly favors ASTER naturalness.
failure_categories: Non-parsable output; framework mismatch; missing imports/package/class/folder; compilation issue; assertion failure; runtime failure.
limitations: Coverage/naturalness-focused system; heterogeneous datasets; not a controlled ChatGPT-vs-Gemini comparison.
rq_relevance: Very high for taxonomy, dependency context and compile/run repair pipeline.

title: AI-Powered Unit Test Generation via Multi-LLM Chaining: A Case Study With GPT-4o, Gemini, and Claude-3.5
objective: Compare single LLMs and multi-LLM chaining for automated Java/JUnit test generation and refinement.
dataset: HumanEval-Java / HumanEval benchmark; 164 programming problems are described; thousands of generated JUnit tests are evaluated.
language_framework: Java / JUnit; Maven or Gradle; JaCoCo; PIT.
models: Gemini; GPT-4o; Claude-3.5 Sonnet; Gemini+GPT-4o; Gemini+Claude-3.5.
prompt_strategy: Source-code metadata extraction; Gemini initial generation; GPT-4o or Claude refinement; validation and coverage feedback.
metrics: Compilation success; runtime test failure/correctness; instruction/branch/line/complexity coverage; mutation coverage.
compile_or_syntax_evidence: Gemini 99.58% compilation success; GPT-4o 99.27%; Claude 99.06%; Gemini+GPT-4o 99.32%; Gemini+Claude 99.01%.
execution_evidence: Runtime failure rates: Gemini 9.78%; Claude 15.01%; GPT-4o 15.28%; Gemini+Claude 10.61%; Gemini+GPT-4o 12.14%.
repair: Multi-model refinement: Gemini generates initial tests; GPT-4o refines edge cases, assertions, inputs and correctness.
main_result: Gemini+GPT-4o achieves 99.05% branch coverage, 90.48% line coverage and 94.32% mutation coverage; single Gemini has the lowest runtime failure rate.
failure_categories: Compilation error; logical inconsistency; invalid assertion; inadequate input coverage; semantic test failure.
limitations: HumanEval/Java/JUnit only; prompt sensitivity; coverage is an incomplete proxy for test quality; extra latency/API cost; no strong significance testing for all claims.
rq_relevance: Extremely high: direct Gemini/GPT-4o + HumanEval-Java/JUnit + separate compile/runtime outcomes.

title: The Impact of Prompt Programming on Function-Level Code Generation
objective: Measure the effect and interaction of five prompt-programming techniques on generated function correctness, similarity and quality.
dataset: CodePromptEval: 221 CoderEval Python tasks × 32 prompt combinations = 7,072 prompts; each run three times.
models: GPT-4o; Llama3-70B-Instruct; Mistral-Small-Instruct-2409; older GPT-3.5/Llama2 data also collected.
prompt_strategy: Full factorial: few-shot, CoT, persona, function signature, package list.
metrics: Pass@k/test correctness; CrystalBLEU similarity; code smells; cyclomatic/cognitive complexity; failure types.
compile_or_syntax_evidence: Syntactic failure is explicitly separated: GPT-4o ~0.4%, Llama3 ~0.9%, Mistral ~1.5% of 7,072 tasks averaged over runs.
execution_evidence: Semantic and operational failures are reported separately; overall pass: GPT-4o 52.2%, Llama3 50.5%, Mistral 46.9%.
repair: No repair loop; study isolates prompt factors.
main_result: Function signature or few-shot context can improve correctness; combining many prompt techniques generally does not reliably improve results. Failure increases with harder dependency levels.
failure_categories: Syntactic; semantic; operational. Task dependency levels: self-contained → project-runnable.
limitations: Function generation rather than test generation; Python rather than Java/JUnit; results depend on CoderEval and selected prompt formulations.
rq_relevance: High methodology support: freeze prompt; classify task/dependency difficulty; do not confound models with prompt variation.

title: On the Effectiveness of LLM-as-a-Judge for Code Generation and Summarization
objective: Assess whether LLMs can reliably judge generated code correctness and code-summary quality.
dataset: CoderEval code generation: 230 Java + 230 Python problems initially; after benchmark QA, 184 Java + 190 Python retained. Code summarization: 1,163 summaries.
language_framework: Java + Python; correctness oracle based on executing benchmark tests.
prompt_strategy: Several judging prompts including zero-shot, rationale, automated CoT and slow-thinking variants.
metrics: Agreement/confusion matrix vs test execution; Cohen's kappa; human agreement for summarization.
compile_or_syntax_evidence: Not a unit-test generation paper; it performs quality assurance on benchmark test suites and generated implementations before judging.
execution_evidence: Test execution is used as the correctness oracle; even GPT-4-turbo frequently misjudges incorrect implementations as correct.
main_result: GPT-4-turbo is the strongest judge but still often misjudges code correctness; execution-based tests remain the more reliable oracle in this setup.
failure_categories: False-positive/false-negative LLM judgement; weak benchmark tests discovered by target/dummy implementation checks.
limitations: Two tasks only; Java/Python only; findings depend on prompt variants and benchmark quality.
rq_relevance: High methodology support: our experiment should use compiler/JUnit execution as ground truth rather than model self-evaluation.
